questions.question: How do you get a 2D drawing context from a <canvas>?
questions.explanation: getContext('2d') returns the CanvasRenderingContext2D used for all drawing commands. 'webgl' returns the 3D context.

questions.question: What does ctx.fillRect(10, 10, 100, 50) draw?

options.text: A 100x50 rectangle whose top-left is at (10,10)

questions.explanation: fillRect(x, y, width, height) fills a rectangle from top-left (x,y). Coordinates are in canvas pixels.

questions.question: Canvas drawing is best described as:
questions.explanation: Canvas is immediate-mode: you issue drawing commands that paint pixels to a bitmap. There's no DOM node per shape (unlike SVG).

questions.question: To handle high-DPI (Retina) displays without blurriness you should:

options.text: Set canvas.width = cssWidth * devicePixelRatio and scale the context
Leave it; canvas is always sharp

questions.explanation: Backing store must match physical pixels: width/height = CSS size * devicePixelRatio, then ctx.scale(ratio, ratio) so drawing coords stay CSS-based.

questions.question: Before redrawing a new frame (animation), you typically call:
questions.explanation: clearRect erases a region so old frames don't smear. Forgetting it is a classic canvas bug.

questions.question: Which library renders charts using <canvas> under the hood?
questions.explanation: Chart.js draws on a canvas element for performant 2D charts. D3 typically uses SVG instead.

questions.question: For GPU-accelerated 3D graphics on canvas you use:
questions.explanation: WebGL provides a separate context (getContext('webgl'/'webgl2')) for hardware-accelerated 3D rendering on the canvas bitmap.

questions.question: Performance best practice for canvas is to:

options.text: Batch drawing ops and minimize state changes
Use one draw call per pixel

questions.explanation: Batching and reducing context state changes (fillStyle swaps, etc.) improves throughput; also consider offscreen canvas.
